newsitem.title: USA: Albright demands results from Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Albright demands results from Arafat.

text.p: Israeli-Palestinian talks this week made headway on security issues but the United States wants to see results from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Wednesday.
"What we have to do is see actions, results," she told reporters.
Albright said she would be going to the Middle East "in the coming days or weeks" but her decision will be based on reports by her expert advisers.

"We consider it essential that the violence be stopped and everything be done by Chairman Arafat to make sure that the infrastructure of the terrorist groups is dismantled and that he make 100 percent effort in order to make sure that the terrorist activities do not take place," she said.
She said last week that her first Middle East trip -- aimed at accelerating peace negotiations -- was conditional on progress in Israeli-Palestinian security coordination.

U.S. envoy Dennis Ross has shuttled between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat since Sunday, managing to bring Israeli and Palestinian security officials together for intelligence sharing.
After speaking by telephone with Ross, Albright said "I believe ... that he has made headway in his talks."

A suicide bombing on July 30 by Muslim militants in the main Jewish market in Jerusalem inflamed a crisis of confidence between Palestinians and Israel, threatening to harm even further already fragile peacemaking.
Palestinians have been angered by unilateral Israeli actions they view as contradictory to peace, especially construction of Jewish settlements in Arab sections of Jerusalem.
But they are also outraged that Israel imposed sanctions on them since the bombing, like withholding transfer of VAT and other taxes owed to the Palestinian Authority.
Netanyahu insisted on Wednesday that Arafat crack down on Muslim militants before such sanctions are eased.
Ross was to fly home to Washington late on Wednesday and U.S. officials said he was expected to meet Albright on Thursday.
Israel's Ambassador to the United States, Eliahu Ben-Elissar, told reporters at a breakfast on Wednesday that Ross, in general, "has been very very successful" on Middle East peacemaking.
"He is the man who is most knowledagble and best informed on Middle Eastern affairs. He has such an immense, impressive amount of information and experience," the envoy added.
